nodes.name: Innovation Ecosystems Model
nodes.description:
- Focuses on creating supportive environments for innovation through the integration of various actors, including startups, research institutions, and investors.
- Promotes the development of networks and infrastructures that facilitate innovation and entrepreneurship.
- Aims to create sustainable and dynamic ecosystems that drive economic growth.

nodes.name: Technological Platforms Model
nodes.description:

- Aims to address common technological challenges and opportunities through shared efforts.
- Focuses on fostering technological advancements and commercialization.

nodes.name: Quadruple Helix Model
nodes.description:
- Extends the Triple Helix Model by incorporating civil society as a key actor in the innovation process.
- Aims to ensure that innovation is socially inclusive and addresses broader societal needs.
- Promotes collaboration between universities, industry, government, and civil society.

nodes.name: Holism

nodes.name: AS-AD Model (Aggregate Supply-Aggregate Demand)

nodes.name: Real Business Cycle (RBC) Model

nodes.name: New Keynesian Models

nodes.name: Overlapping Generations (OLG) Models

nodes.name: Argentina
nodes.description: A federal presidential republic and the second-largest country in South America. Defined by its immigrant heritage, complex federal structure, and oscillation between developmentalist and neoliberal economic models.

nodes.name: Australia
nodes.description: Australia is a federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy and the only country that is also a continent. A resource-exporting powerhouse deeply tied to Indo-Pacific demand, it combines mining and agriculture with advanced services, education exports and a large pension-capital pool. Six states and two territories share power under a stable federal system.

nodes.name: Brazil
nodes.description: Brazil is a federal presidential republic in South America and the largest country in both area and population in the region. It possesses a diversified economy spanning agriculture, mining, manufacturing, and services, and plays a central geopolitical and ecological role due to the Amazon rainforest and its membership in major multilateral groupings.

nodes.name: Canada
nodes.description: Canada is a federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy and the world's second-largest country by area. A Commonwealth realm with English-French bilingualism, it combines vast natural-resource endowments with an advanced services economy deeply integrated with the United States. Key sectors include energy, mining, forestry, banking and technology, under a decentralized federal system.

nodes.name: China
nodes.description: China is Party-State polity in East Asia and the world's most populous major state. Governed by a single-party system under the Chinese Communist Party, it has transformed over the past four decades from a largely agrarian economy into a global industrial and technological power. China plays a central role in global manufacturing, trade, infrastructure development, and emerging technologies.

nodes.name: Denmark
nodes.description: Denmark is a parliamentary constitutional monarchy in Northern Europe and a pioneer of wind energy. Its Nordic welfare model pairs flexible labor markets with broad social protection, while the economy specializes in pharmaceuticals, shipping, food and design. An EU member outside the eurozone, it anchors the Realm community with Greenland and the Faroe Islands.

nodes.name: Dominican Republic
nodes.description: The Dominican Republic is a sovereign presidential republic on the island of Hispaniola in the Caribbean, sharing its territory with Haiti. Historically shaped by sugarcane, mining, and tourism, it has evolved into a dynamic economy with strong remittance inflows, diversified services and industrial sectors, and growing investments in renewable energy and infrastructure.

nodes.name: England
nodes.description: England is a constituent country of the United Kingdom located in Western Europe. It was the core territorial and institutional base of the early modern English state and later the British Empire. England played a central role in the Industrial Revolution, the development of parliamentary governance, common law traditions, and the formation of modern financial and industrial capitalism.

nodes.name: Finland
nodes.description: Finland is a unitary parliamentary republic in Northern Europe and a global reference for education. Independent since 1917, it transformed from forestry dependence into an ICT and engineering economy led by Nokia-era successors, while retaining strong welfare institutions. EU and eurozone membership, plus 2023 NATO accession, frame its open, innovation-driven economy.

nodes.name: France
nodes.description: France is a unitary semi-presidential republic and the European Union's second-largest economy. Combining a strong central state with global cultural influence, it leads in aerospace, luxury goods, nuclear energy and agriculture. EU integration, high public investment and a large welfare state shape its coordinated market economy.

nodes.name: Hong Kong
nodes.description: Hong Kong is a Special Administrative Region of the People’s Republic of China, located on the southern coast of China. It has a highly developed, service-oriented economy, historically rooted in trade, finance, and logistics. Hong Kong is a major global financial center and port, with strong legal and regulatory institutions inherited from its colonial history under the United Kingdom. In recent years, there has been a push to develop technology and innovation sectors alongside traditional …

nodes.name: India
nodes.description: India is a sovereign federal parliamentary republic in South Asia and the world’s most populous country. It combines a long civilizational history with modern constitutional governance established in 1950. India has a structurally diversified economy spanning agriculture, manufacturing, and a globally competitive services and technology sector, and plays an increasingly central role in Indo-Pacific geopolitics and multilateral institutions.

nodes.name: Indonesia
nodes.description: Indonesia is a sovereign archipelagic republic in Southeast Asia composed of more than 17,000 islands. It is the world’s largest Muslim-majority country and one of the most populous nations globally. Indonesia has a diversified economy based on natural resources, manufacturing, and services, and plays a central geopolitical role within ASEAN and the broader Indo-Pacific region.

nodes.name: Ireland
nodes.description: Ireland is a sovereign parliamentary republic in Western Europe occupying most of the island of Ireland. Since the late 20th century, it has transformed into a high-income, small open economy characterized by strong foreign direct investment inflows, a competitive corporate tax regime, and specialization in pharmaceuticals, information technology, and financial services within the European Union framework.

nodes.name: Israel
nodes.description: Israel is a unitary parliamentary republic in the Middle East known for its technology and defense sectors. Founded in 1948, it built a startup-nation economy on R&D intensity, venture capital and military-civilian technology transfer, alongside strengths in water, agriculture and diamonds. Regional conflict and disputed borders remain central to its political economy.

nodes.name: Italy
nodes.description: Italy is a unitary parliamentary republic and a founding member of the European Communities. Its economy pairs northern industrial districts — machinery, automotive, fashion — with a vast cultural-heritage tourism sector and persistent southern structural challenges. A G7 economy in the eurozone, it balances manufacturing excellence with high public debt and demographic aging.

nodes.name: Japan
nodes.description: Japan is a parliamentary constitutional monarchy and one of the world's largest economies. Postwar industrial policy produced global leaders in automotive, electronics and robotics, organized around keiretsu networks and coordinated business-government councils. It now navigates rapid demographic aging, high public debt and energy import dependence while leading in automation and materials science.

nodes.name: Malaysia
nodes.description: Malaysia is a federal constitutional monarchy in Southeast Asia composed of Peninsular Malaysia and East Malaysian states on the island of Borneo. Since independence, it has transitioned from a commodity-based economy to an export-oriented manufacturing and services hub, with strong specialization in electronics, palm oil, and petroleum, supported by industrial policy and integration into regional and global value chains.

nodes.name: Mexico
nodes.description: Mexico is a federal presidential republic and Latin America's second-largest economy. Deeply integrated with the United States through USMCA supply chains, it is a manufacturing hub for automotive, electronics and aerospace alongside oil, mining and massive remittance inflows. Thirty-one states plus Mexico City share power in a democratic federal system consolidated since 2000.

nodes.name: Netherlands
nodes.description: The Netherlands is a constitutional monarchy in Western Europe known for its advanced, trade-oriented economy and long-standing maritime and commercial tradition. Historically central to early modern global trade and finance, it remains a major logistics and distribution hub within Europe, with strong sectors in agriculture, chemicals, high-tech manufacturing, and financial services.

nodes.name: New Zealand
nodes.description: New Zealand is a sovereign island nation in Oceania composed primarily of the North and South Islands. It operates as a parliamentary democracy and constitutional monarchy. Historically shaped by Māori settlement and later British colonization, New Zealand developed a high-income, export-oriented economy centered on agriculture, agri-technology, tourism, and services, with strong institutional quality and regulatory transparency.

nodes.name: Ottoman Empire
nodes.description: The Ottoman Empire (1299–1922) was a transcontinental Islamic empire centered on Anatolia, the Balkans and the Middle East, ruled by a sultan-caliph from Constantinople. At its early modern peak it commanded major Eurasian trade routes and a tributary provincial order. Military defeat, nationalist secessions and World War I reduced it to Anatolia, ending with the Turkish Republic's proclamation in 1923. Figures below are a c.1914 snapshot.

nodes.name: Portugal
nodes.description: Portugal is a unitary semi-presidential republic on the Iberian Peninsula's Atlantic edge and one of Europe's oldest nation-states. Pioneer of the Age of Discovery with a deep seafaring and mercantile tradition, it moved from dictatorship to democracy with the 1974 Carnation Revolution and joined the European Communities in 1986. Its open economy leans on services, tourism, cork, wine and olive oil, with fast-growing technology and renewable-energy sectors.

nodes.name: Scotland
nodes.description: Scotland is a devolved nation within the United Kingdom with its own parliament, legal system and distinct cultural identity. Center of the Enlightenment and nineteenth-century heavy industry, it now blends North Sea energy, whisky and food exports, financial services in Edinburgh, and growing renewables. Devolution since 1999 gives Holyrood powers over health, education and justice.

nodes.name: Singapore
nodes.description: Singapore is a sovereign city-state at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula and one of the world's leading trade and financial hubs. Independent since 1965 after separation from Malaysia, it built prosperity on its strategic strait-side port, rule of law, and openness to capital and talent. Its advanced economy centers on shipping and logistics, financial services, electronics and petrochemicals, with a state-guided development model.

nodes.name: South Korea
nodes.description: South Korea is a sovereign presidential republic in East Asia located on the southern portion of the Korean Peninsula. Following the Korean War, it transitioned from a low-income agrarian economy to a high-income, export-oriented industrial and technological power. Its development model combined state-led industrial policy, chaebol-centered conglomerate growth, human capital accumulation, and deep integration into global value chains.

nodes.name: Spain
nodes.description: Spain is a parliamentary constitutional monarchy in Southern Europe and one of the eurozone's largest economies. Restored to democracy after Franco's death in 1975 and an EU member since 1986, it is organized as a highly decentralized state of autonomous communities. Tourism, automotive manufacturing, banking and renewable energy anchor an open, services-led economy.

nodes.name: Sweden
nodes.description: Sweden is a constitutional monarchy in Northern Europe characterized by a high-income, export-oriented economy and a comprehensive welfare state. Historically transitioning from agrarian society to industrial power in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, Sweden developed globally competitive firms in engineering, automotive, telecommunications, and life sciences, supported by strong institutions, human capital formation, and social partnership models.

nodes.name: Switzerland
nodes.description: Switzerland is a neutral federal republic renowned for direct democracy, banking and precision industries. Its consensus-driven cantonal federalism underpins political stability and openness, hosting global finance, pharmaceuticals, watchmaking and commodity trading. Outside the EU but deeply integrated via bilateral accords, it runs persistent surpluses on high-value services and manufacturing.

nodes.name: Thailand
nodes.description: Thailand is a constitutional monarchy in Southeast Asia with a diversified, export-oriented economy. Historically the Kingdom of Siam, it avoided formal colonization and underwent gradual modernization in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Since the late 20th century, Thailand has developed strong manufacturing sectors—particularly automotive and electronics—alongside tourism and agro-industrial exports, integrated into regional and global value chains.

nodes.name: United Arab Emirates
nodes.description: The United Arab Emirates is a federal monarchy of seven emirates on the Arabian Gulf's southern shore. Since federation in 1971, oil wealth has funded diversification into finance, aviation, logistics and tourism, with Dubai and Abu Dhabi as global hubs. Its open, expatriate-majority economy pairs sovereign-wealth investment with ambitious technology and energy-transition bets.

nodes.name: United States
nodes.description: The United States is a federal presidential republic and the world's largest economy, spanning North America from the Atlantic to the Pacific. Founded on constitutional federalism with separation of powers, it became the center of twentieth-century industrial, financial and technological power. Its economy leads in technology, capital markets, higher education and defense industries, with the dollar as the global reserve currency.

nodes.name: Uruguay
nodes.description: Uruguay is a sovereign presidential republic in South America located between Brazil and Argentina along the Atlantic coast. Historically shaped by livestock-based exports and early welfare-state development, it has evolved into a relatively stable democracy with strong institutions, diversified agricultural exports, growing services sectors, and a high share of renewable energy generation in its electricity matrix.

nodes.name: Vietnam
nodes.description: Vietnam is a One-Party State polity located in Southeast Asia, bordered by China, Laos, and Cambodia, with an extensive coastline along the South China Sea. It operates under a one-party system led by the Communist Party of Vietnam. Historically shaped by Chinese rule, French colonization, and the Vietnam War, the country has transitioned into a rapidly growing emerging economy with key sectors including agriculture, manufacturing, electronics, and services. Institutional development and …

nodes.name: Reality
nodes.description: The ontological substrate comprising physical, chemical, biological, informational, and social structures that constrain and respond to technical intervention.

nodes.name: Action Interface & Actuation
nodes.description: The motoric and encoding boundary through which an agent imparts energy, information, or structure onto reality.

nodes.name: Concrete Technical Artifact
nodes.description: A specific, fully-specified object, system, or code module that has been produced or operated; the primary carrier of technical effect.

nodes.name: Technical Blueprint
nodes.description: Generative description that prescribes how to create, assemble, or configure an artifact.

nodes.name: Technical Agent
nodes.description: Entity that executes technical operations by utilizing tools, energy, and instructions.

nodes.name: Technical Process
nodes.description: Ordered sequence of technical acts that transform inputs into outputs.

nodes.name: Technical Standard
nodes.description: Normative specification that governs form, fit, function, safety, or performance.

nodes.name: Technical Constraint
nodes.description: Bound on achievable action imposed by physical law, material properties, resource availability, or regulation.

nodes.name: Technical Infrastructure
nodes.description: Ambient capital—material, energetic, informational, institutional—that makes sustained technical practice possible.

nodes.name: Technical Feedback
nodes.description: Signal that indicates real-world effect of a technical act, enabling adjustment and error correction.

nodes.name: Technical Act
nodes.description: Primitive, non-decomposable operation that a technical agent performs on reality or an artifact.

nodes.name: Technical Principle
nodes.description: Foundational design law, operating axiom, or reliability rule governing technical interventions.

nodes.name: Technical Strategy
nodes.description: Context-sensitive, resource-aware regime of planning and decision-making organizing technical work.

nodes.name: Technical Framework
nodes.description: Overarching problem-structuring and solution-generation logic within which technical agents interpret requirements and synthesize artifacts.

nodes.name: Technical Operator
nodes.description: Formal, procedural, or physical mechanism used to transform, assemble, verify, or maintain technical artifacts.

nodes.name: Production Technical Object
nodes.description: Final deployable artifact that fulfills ultimate technical purpose in its operational environment.

nodes.name: Constitutive Technical Object
nodes.description: Intermediate artifact, component, or sub-assembly serving as building block within a larger production object.

nodes.name: Technique
nodes.description: Generalized, culturally transmitted body of knowledge regarding how to achieve a specific type of technical effect.

nodes.name: Operative Technique
nodes.description: Context-specific, situated application of a generalized technique by a technical agent.

nodes.name: Constitutive Technique
nodes.description: Specialized methods dedicated to creation, testing, and integration of constitutive technical objects.

nodes.name: Technical Purpose
nodes.description: Teleological orientation of an artifact or process; the intended ultimate impact on reality, human experience, or a broader system.

references.title: The Structure of Technical Practice – A Teleological Framework

nodes.name: Technical Architecture
nodes.description: Fundamental structural organization of a system, embodied in its components, their relationships, and design principles.

nodes.name: Technical Specification
nodes.description: Precise, quantitative statement of technical requirements, performance parameters, and interface conditions.

nodes.name: Technical Evolution
nodes.description: Cumulative historical trajectory of change in technical artifacts, processes, or knowledge over time.

nodes.name: Technical Labor
nodes.description: Purposive expenditure of human cognitive and physical effort applied to technical processes.

nodes.name: Technical Institution
nodes.description: Formalized, durable social structures that organize, govern, incentivize, and sustain technical practice.

nodes.name: Technical Research
nodes.description: Systematic investigation aimed at discovering new technical principles, materials, processes, or capabilities.

nodes.name: Technical Competence
nodes.description: Embodied, acquired capacity of a technical agent to reliably execute technical processes and operative techniques.

nodes.name: Technical Failure
nodes.description: State or event wherein an artifact or process deviates from its technical specification or required function.

nodes.name: Technical Requirement
nodes.description: Formalized desired state, need, or performance objective that initiates technical practice.

nodes.name: Verification
nodes.description: Systematic process to evaluate whether an artifact fulfills its technical specification or blueprint.

nodes.name: Maintenance
nodes.description: Ordered set of technical acts performed to retain or restore an artifact to a state where it can reliably perform its function.

nodes.name: Security
nodes.description: Domain of principles, constraints, and processes protecting a system from unauthorized access, disruption, or destruction.

nodes.name: Resource
nodes.description: Consumable or non-consumable inputs—matter, energy, information, time, capital—required, transformed, or consumed by technical practice.

nodes.name: Decision Problem

nodes.name: Structural Causal Model (SCM)

nodes.name: Utility Function

nodes.name: Epistemic Act
nodes.description: Primitive, non‑decomposable operation performed by an agent.

nodes.name: Epistemic Agent
nodes.description: Entity that performs epistemic operations by applying tools to artifacts.

nodes.name: Epistemic Artifact
nodes.description: Structured object that encodes claims, constraints, or distributions over reality; the primary carrier of semantic content.

nodes.name: Epistemic Constraint
nodes.description: Limitation that bounds what can be known or inferred within the system.

nodes.name: Epistemic Domain (Segment of Reality)
nodes.description: Segment of reality that the epistemic practice targets or models.

nodes.name: Epistemic Feedback

nodes.name: Epistemic Infrastructure

nodes.name: Interpretation Layer
nodes.description: Interpretation function that assigns meaning to an epistemic artifact.

nodes.name: Meta‑Epistemic Layer

nodes.name: Observation Interface & Recoding

nodes.name: Epistemic Process (Activity)

nodes.name: Epistemic Standard
nodes.description: Normative criteria used to evaluate validity, correctness, or acceptability of artifacts and processes.

nodes.name: Encoding Substrate
nodes.description: Encoding format or substrate in which artifacts are expressed; constrains manipulation and interpretation.

nodes.name: Epistemic Tool
nodes.description: Formal or procedural mechanism used to construct, transform, or validate epistemic artifacts.

nodes.name: Number

nodes.name: Confounder

references.title: No Free Lunch Theorems for Optimization

nodes.name: No-go Theorem

nodes.name: Uncertainty Constraint
nodes.description: A limiting condition in which incomplete or stochastic information restricts the determinacy of inference and decision outcomes.
